content: 1. In May 2018, the drug was discontinued from the market as it had been largely replaced by newer medications with higher cure rates. Its safety and efficacy were not well-established. 2. Levoketoconazole increases the levels of simeprevir by interfering with the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is advised to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Simeprevir increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Serious symptomatic bradycardia has been reported in patients taking amiodarone who initiate treatment with sofosbuvir in combination with another HCV direct-acting antiviral, including simeprevir. This is particularly concerning in patients on beta blockers, those with underlying cardiac comorbidities, or those with advanced liver disease. Co-administration of amiodarone with simeprevir and sofosbuvir is not recommended. If no alternative treatment options are available, cardiac monitoring is advised. 5. Hepatic decompensation and hepatic failure, including fatal cases, have been reported in patients receiving therapy with simeprevir in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin or sofosbuvir. Most cases occurred in patients with advanced or decompensated cirrhosis, who are at increased risk for hepatic decompensation or failure. Liver chemistry tests should be monitored before and during simeprevir combination therapy. 6. Photosensitivity reactions, including serious cases requiring hospitalization, have been reported. Rash may occur, most frequently within the first four weeks of treatment. Mild-to-moderate rashes should be monitored for progression, including the development of mucosal signs (e.g., oral lesions, conjunctivitis) or systemic symptoms. Treatment should be discontinued if the rash becomes severe. 7. Simeprevir contains a sulfonamide moiety. In a small study of patients with a history of sulfa allergy, no increased incidence of rash or photosensitivity reactions was observed. However, data are insufficient to draw definitive conclusions. 8. Simeprevir must not be used as monotherapy. It is co-administered with ribavirin and peginterferon alfa. Extreme caution must be taken to avoid pregnancy in female patients and female partners of male patients during this combination therapy. 9. Ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant, as it may cause birth defects and fetal death. Women of childbearing potential and their male partners should use effective contraception (two reliable forms) during treatment with ribavirin and for six months after treatment. A negative pregnancy test is required before initiating therapy. 10. Ribavirin has demonstrated significant teratogenic and embryocidal effects in all animal species studied. Therefore, it is contraindicated in women of childbearing potential unless effective contraception is used. 11. It is unknown whether simeprevir is distributed in human breast milk. Due to the potential for adverse reactions in nursing infants, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. 12. All patients should be tested for evidence of current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection before initiating treatment with HCV direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). HBV reactivation has been reported in HCV/HBV co-infected patients undergoing or having completed DAA therapy without concurrent HBV antiviral therapy. Some cases have resulted in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death. HCV/HBV co-infected patients should be monitored for hepatitis flare or HBV reactivation during HCV treatment and post-treatment follow-up. Appropriate management for HBV infection should be initiated as clinically indicated. 13. Simeprevir in combination with ribavirin and peginterferon alfa is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant due to the risk of birth defects and fetal death. Patients must have a negative pregnancy test prior to therapy and use two or more forms of contraception during treatment and for six months afterward. One form of contraception can be a combined oral contraceptive containing at least 1 mg of norethindrone, as lower doses and other forms of hormonal contraception have not been studied or are contraindicated. 14. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, and the drug is generally considered acceptable in this context.
